## A trunk that gets thicker

A young neem tree has a trunk about as thick as your wrist. Twenty years later, the same trunk is as thick as a bucket.

**Predict:** How does the trunk get thicker?

options.text: The cells already in the trunk stretch and swell, so the same cells fill a wider trunk.
A ring of dividing cells in the stem keeps adding new cells, layer after layer.
The tip of the stem makes new cells, which slide down and wrap around the trunk.
The leaves send new cells down the trunk, where they pile up on the outside.
